bib.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; all body, tables and appendices A-I read.

question: Can a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe that combines a pre-trained seq2seq generator (parametric memory) with a dense Wikipedia index accessed by a pre-trained retriever (non-parametric memory) improve knowledge-intensive NLP tasks?
hypothesis: Hybrid parametric plus non-parametric memory, trained end-to-end with retrieved documents as latent variables, beats parametric-only seq2seq models and task-specific retrieve-and-extract systems, and gives updatable, inspectable knowledge.
contributions: RAG, a general fine-tuning recipe combining pre-trained parametric (BART) and non-parametric (DPR + Wikipedia index) memory for generation
Two formulations, RAG-Sequence (one document per output) and RAG-Token (different document per token)
State of the art on open-domain QA (NQ, WQ, CT; TQA on the T5-comparable split) and more factual, specific, diverse generation than BART
Retrieval ablations and index hot-swapping showing the knowledge can be updated without retraining

method.summary: The retriever (DPR bi-encoder, BERT-base query and document encoders) returns top-K Wikipedia passages by MIPS; BART-large conditions on input concatenated with each passage; outputs are marginalised over passages (per sequence or per token). Query encoder and generator are fine-tuned end-to-end by negative marginal log-likelihood while the document encoder and index stay fixed.
method.task: knowledge-intensive NLP: open-domain QA, abstractive QA (MS-MARCO), Jeopardy question generation, FEVER fact verification

datasets.name: Wikipedia dump December 2018 (non-parametric memory)
datasets.size: 21M documents of disjoint 100-word chunks; 21M 728-dim vectors (15.3B values)
datasets.source: Lee et al. / Karpukhin et al. dump
datasets.preprocessing: articles split into disjoint 100-word chunks; FAISS MIPS index with HNSW approximation

datasets.name: Natural Questions
datasets.preprocessing: each (q,a) pair of multiple annotations trained separately

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.split: DPR splits; test = public TriviaQA Web dev split; also official TQA-Wiki test
datasets.preprocessing: answer candidates dropped if not in top 1000 documents for the query

datasets.name: WebQuestions
datasets.preprocessing: model initialised from NQ RAG model

datasets.name: CuratedTrec
datasets.preprocessing: regex answers: top 1000 docs retrieved, most frequent regex match used as target, else permutation heuristic; initialised from NQ RAG model

datasets.name: MS-MARCO NLG v2.1
datasets.split: questions and answers only, gold passages not used

datasets.name: FEVER
datasets.preprocessing: labels mapped to single output tokens; no retrieval supervision

models.name: RAG-Sequence
models.params: 626M trainable (110M query encoder + 406M BART-large + 110M document encoder not trained; paper's own sum)
models.architecture: DPR bi-encoder retriever + BART-large, sequence-level marginalisation

other.note: text states BART-large as 400M in 2.3 and 406M in Appendix G

models.name: DPR retriever
models.architecture: bi-encoder, p(z|x) proportional to exp(d(z)^T q(x))
models.init_from: DPR trained on TriviaQA and Natural Questions

other.note: trained by the authors as parametric-only baseline for generation tasks

training.objective: minimise negative marginal log-likelihood sum_j -log p(y_j|x_j); no supervision on which document to retrieve
training.hardware: 8 x 32GB NVIDIA V100 GPUs (training and inference can run on one GPU)

other.frozen: document encoder BERT_d and index kept fixed; only query encoder BERT_q and BART generator fine-tuned
other.k_train: k in {5,10} documents retrieved during training; k at test chosen on dev
other.framework: Fairseq; later ported to HuggingFace Transformers with equivalent performance
other.index_memory: ~100 GB CPU memory for all of Wikipedia; 36GB after FAISS compression
other.init: CT and WQ models initialised from the NQ RAG model

inference.decoding: QA: greedy decoding; MS-MARCO and Jeopardy: beam size four. RAG-Token: standard beam decoder on marginalised token distribution. RAG-Sequence: Thorough Decoding (QA) or Fast Decoding (generation)
inference.samples: single run per model reported; no seeds or variance stated
inference.prompting: input x concatenated with retrieved passage z as BART input
inference.retrieval: top-k by MIPS over FAISS HNSW index. QA test: 15 docs RAG-Token, 50 docs RAG-Sequence; MS-MARCO and Jeopardy: 10 docs for both

metrics.name: Q-BLEU-1
metrics.definition: SQuAD-tuned variant of BLEU weighting entity matches

metrics.name: Human pairwise factuality/specificity
metrics.definition: annotators see answer and two questions (BART vs RAG) and pick A, B, both good, neither good

metrics.name: Distinct/total tri-grams
metrics.definition: ratio of distinct to total tri-grams

baselines: task SotA (PALM for MS-MARCO, FEVER-3 Zhong et al., FEVER-2 Thorne and Vlachos)
eval.protocol: Single reported runs; no significance tests stated. Human eval: 452 pairs, random A/B order, annotators may research online, gold sentences used and two poor annotators removed.

availability.weights: HuggingFace demo at https://huggingface.co/rag/ (weights not explicitly stated)

RAG-Sequence gets 68.0 EM on the TQA-Wiki test set (T5-11B+SSM 60.5) and 56.8 on the standard TQA test (DPR 57.9).

results.claim: RAG-Sequence scores 52.2 EM on CuratedTrec and 45.2 on WebQuestions.
results.setup: CT test, init from NQ RAG model

FEVER 2-way: RAG-Token 89.5, within 2.7% of RoBERTa given gold evidence (92.2).

results.claim: Freezing the retriever lowers NQ dev EM from 44.0 to 41.2 for RAG-Sequence; BM25 gives 31.8.
BM25 beats learned dense retrieval on FEVER-3 (75.1 vs 74.5 for RAG-Token), but dense is better on other tasks, especially open-domain QA.
results.setup: dev set, RAG-Token-BM25 vs RAG-Token, FVR-3

results.quote:
RAG answers 70% correctly using the 2016 index for

results.quote:
Accuracy with mismatched

results.claim: T5-large (770M) gets 28.9 EM on NQ versus 44.5 for RAG-Sequence (626M trainable parameters).
results.quote:
which achieves a score of 28.9 EM on Natural Questions [52],
substantially below the 44.5 that RAG-Sequence achieves

results.claim: Retrieving more docs at test time monotonically improves open-domain QA for RAG-Sequence, while RAG-Token peaks at 10.
results.setup: NQ, K retrieved docs varied, Fig 3 (left)

results.claim: Retrieval collapse: on tasks such as story generation the retriever learned to return the same documents regardless of input and RAG matched BART.

limits: Learning rate, schedule, batch size, steps/epochs, dropout, seeds and wall-clock are not stated; training is not reproducible from the paper alone.
Single runs, no variance or significance tests; MS-MARCO test is a hidden subset.
Retriever initialised from DPR trained with retrieval supervision on NQ and TriviaQA; document encoder and index frozen.
Wikipedia (Dec 2018) is not entirely factual or bias-free; misuse risks conceded in Broader Impact.
Retrieval collapse on some tasks (story generation); null-document mechanisms tried and dropped.
FEVER evidence-retrieval sub-task not tackled; RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence need different k and decoding.
TriviaQA SotA only on the T5-comparable split; official Wiki test set is easier.
Joint pre-training of both components left as future work.
Human factuality measured by annotators allowed to research online; 20.8% of pairs had no majority.
